page: Amazon Web Services trn2.3xlarge is a specialized accelerated computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and engineered specifically for machine learning workloads. The system features a single AWS Trainium2 accelerator paired with 96 GB of dedicated VRAM, making it tailored for deep learning training and large language model inference. On the host compute side, the instance provides 12 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 6 physical Intel cores clocked at 3.5 GHz, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 10.67 GB per physical core.

The instance includes bundled local storage consisting of a 470 GB NVMe SSD, providing low-latency ephemeral scratch space for dataset staging, intermediate checkpointing, and caching. Complementing the compute and storage resources, the trn2.3xlarge delivers a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. This network capacity facilitates efficient distributed data transfer and cluster synchronization. Note that complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

In terms of cost efficiency, the integration of custom AWS Trainium2 silicon offers a purpose-built alternative to general-purpose GPUs, optimizing resource expenditure specifically for ML model execution. The hardware profile is best suited for targeted deep learning model training, fine-tuning tasks, and high-throughput model inference pipelines requiring high accelerator memory capacity alongside solid host memory and fast local NVMe storage.
